source.title: Establishing Best Practices for Building Rigorous Agentic Benchmarks

O.a.1.definition: Considers expressions semantically equivalent to ground truth.

O.a.2.definition: Handles redundant words used by agents.

O.b.1.definition: Handles negation modifiers used by agents.

O.b.2.definition: Is robust against systematically listing all possible answers.

O.b.3.definition: Ground truth is sufficiently complex to prevent guessing.

O.c.1.definition: Demonstrates documented or experimental evidence of the judge’s accuracy, self-consistency, and agreement with human.

O.c.2.definition: Is designed to resist adversarial inputs and reward hacking.

O.d.1.definition: Verifies test cases for correctness and quality (e.g., by human).

O.d.2.definition: Measures quality of test cases using objective metrics (e.g., code coverage, cyclomatic complexity control).

O.e.2.definition: Ensures comprehensive coverage of all relevant input variations (e.g., data types, memory layouts, value ranges).

O.e.3.definition: Generates inputs that the code under testing is sensitive to.

O.f.1.definition: Exercises all relevant parts of the code being tested.

O.g.1.definition: Ground truth includes all states achievable after success.

O.g.2.definition: Checks relevant and irrelevant states for the challenge.

O.g.3.definition: Ground truth is complex to prevent trivial state modifications.

O.h.1.definition: Specifies required answer formats in challenge descriptions.

O.h.2.definition: Minimizes the possibility of success by random guessing.

O.i.1.definition: Designs quality metrics that prevent exploitation (e.g., achieving high scores by reward hacking).

T.1.definition: Versions of all tools (e.g., Python) are clearly specified.

T.2.definition: Required API tools are consistently accessible during evaluation.

T.3.definition: Evaluation process terminates or handles errors appropriately if an API becomes inaccessible.

T.4.definition: Residual data or state are fully cleared between runs.

T.5.definition: Agent is completely isolated from any ground truth information.

T.6.definition: Setup does not change over time (e.g., no live website).

T.7.definition: Annotated ground truth is verified for correctness.

T.8.definition: Each task is verified to be solvable.

T.9.definition: Benchmark includes an Oracle solver that can automatically solve all challenges.

T.10.definition: Implementation is free of vulnerabilities that could be exploited to pass evaluations without completing tasks.

R.1.definition: Is fully or at least partially open-sourced.

R.2.definition: Offers an open-source evaluation harness for users.

R.3.definition: Includes measures to prevent data contamination at the time of benchmark release, such as a private, held-out test set.

R.4.definition: Includes measures or plans to consistently update challenges over time to avoid overfitting.

R.5.definition: Clearly states the relationship between the agent capabilities it aims to evaluate and the constructs or outcomes it measures.

R.6.definition: Clearly states the evaluation subjective of the benchmark (e.g., a model or an agent framework).

R.7.definition: Describes steps taken to prevent, identify, and correct flaws.

R.8.definition: Includes qualitative discussions of the potential impact of unavoidable flaws.

R.9.definition: Includes quantitative analysis to assess the impact of unavoidable flaws (e.g., noise of ground truth).

R.10.definition: Reports metrics about statistical significance, such as confidence intervals.

R.11.definition: Provides guidance on interpreting results with eval flaws.

R.12.definition: Reports results of non-AI baselines (e.g., human experts).

R.13.definition: Reports results of trivial agents (e.g., one that does nothing).
